chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Abu Dawud together, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ali ibn Abi Jahmat, from Jahm ibn Humayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
My father (peace be upon him) used to say: 'When Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) stood for prayer, he was like the trunk of a tree; nothing moved from him except what the wind moved from him.'
ai.seo_question: How did the Imams demonstrate humility and stillness during prayer?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kulayni’s *al-Kafi* within the chapter on humility in prayer, this narration highlights the physical manifestation of *khushu’* (devotional focus) through the serene stability of Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn. The metaphor of the tree trunk underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on inner tranquility reflecting in outward stillness, distinguishing deep contemplation from mere mechanical movement. This exemplifies the ideal state of *iqamah* (standing) where the believer’s body becomes a vessel for divine presence, free from distracting frivolities.
